applies_to: Titus Digital T3SQ diffuser networks where an MCU 2 master comms unit gathers up to 60 master-diffuser zones for a BMS.
summary: The MCU 2 is the network gateway for the Titus Digital T3SQ diffuser system: it reports up to 60 diffuser control zones to a BMS as BACnet/IP (part BW2011-2B) or BACnet MS/TP (BW2011-2M). Each object type is laid out as blocks of 60 instances, one per zone, so instance = block start + zone - 1. Only master-diffuser data is available; slave diffusers and detailed setup or diagnostics are not exposed. Zones that are not set up on the MCU simply return no data.
default_device_instance: Derived from the Ethernet MAC address (BACnet/IP); editable
notes: The source gives instance ranges (e.g. AV:0..59 = Space Temp 1..60); individual object names here follow that pattern and may differ slightly on the device.
Access is inferred: analog/multistate inputs and values as read-only, AO setpoints and MSO commands as commandable (the stack has a 16-level priority array).
Temperature units can be switched between °C and °F on the MCU web page; the table lists °C ranges.
The MCU web page also lists global points (averaged disk position and room temperature, global setpoint/override); their instances are not in the document.

source.title: Titus Digital T3SQ MLM Integration with BMS

integration.summary: Discover the MCU 2 (one BACnet device for up to 60 zones) and map each zone by offset: zone n is instance n-1 in the first block of each type. Write the zone setpoint to the AO block and use the two MSO blocks for flush/emergency commands and occupancy override, after enabling Control Override on each zone master with the MLM Tool.

minimum_points.name: Control override 1
minimum_points.why: Zone 1 BMS control override such as flush or emergency (MSO 0-59)

integration.enable: BMS commands (control override and occupancy override MSOs) only take effect after Control Override is ticked on the master diffuser of that zone in the MLM Tool (Process / Master Command, then Write). That setting is non-volatile. Write 1 (Normal) to release a command.
integration.remote_sensors: Only the zone setpoint (AO 0-59) is written from the BMS; there is no BMS-fed temperature input in the point map.
setup: BACnet/IP: default MCU IP address 192.168.0.251; device name, BACnet ID and BACnet UDP port are set on the MCU web page (Save).
Holding BOOT until ST1 flashes, then pressing DEF, resets the MCU to the default IP address.
BACnet MS/TP: default MAC 25 (range 0-127), default baud 76800; checked and set over USB with the MLM Tool (V8.xx required).
BACnet has to be activated on the MCU with a key (normally done at the factory); the web page shows the BACnet state.
ReadPropertyMultiple/WritePropertyMultiple are supported; segmentation is not; max APDU 480 bytes.
gotchas: Instances start at 0, so zone n is instance n-1 (plus the block offset).
Multistate values are shown as numbers on many front ends; read State_Text for the labels.
A generic BACnet reader shows all 60 zones whether populated or not; unpopulated zones carry no data.
Slave diffusers mimic their master; no per-slave points are exposed.
